mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
reason: whole: The order waives, for one named employee, the limit in section 1 of EO 9721 on the period treated as leave of absence and deems him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purposes of EO 9721, as amended. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"). EO 10804 of 1959-02-12 had already revoked EO 9721 and EO 10103 subject to savings, including for rights and benefits vested before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act; that revocation precedes this order and is not its end. The waiver took effect on the order's own date (1966-09-12), a disclosed alternative reading of exhaustion that is not adopted as the end because the deeming operates for the rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, as amended, which remained in effect under EO 10804's saving for vested rights and benefits until EO 12553 revoked EO 9721 on the same day. The surviving consequence is recorded under savings.
